slides.title: All About Bugs
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 2 English, Unit 6: All About Bugs. In this unit you explore the tiny world of bugs, insects and other small garden animals. You learn the names of the butterfly, cricket, ant, bee, spider and worm, and you find out what makes an animal an insect: six legs, three body parts and two antennae. You learn position words such as on, under, between and above so that you can say exactly where a creature is, and you use the simple present tense to give true facts. By the end you can describe a creature of your own, just like Amal in this unit's story, “Amal and the Little Garden Friends”. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name common bugs and garden animals: butterfly, cricket, ant, bee, spider and worm.
Say what makes an animal an insect: six legs, three body parts and two antennae.
Explain why a spider and a worm are not insects.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name common bugs and garden animals: butterfly, cricket, ant, bee, spider and worm. You will also say what makes an animal an insect: six legs, three body parts and two antennae. You will also explain why a spider and a worm are not insects. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: turn, burn, hurt, shirt, pretty, rock. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes What Is an Insect? and A Bug Poem. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Position Words. Position words tell us where something is. When we watch bugs we need them to say exactly where each creature sits: on a leaf, under a rock, or inside a hole. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Speaking 1 — Name and Describe a Bug
Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Name and Describe a Bug. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
